description: Stop doing the mirror wrong: daily grades, borrowed comparisons and memory as the archive. Retest mirror versus scale, then train your body composition tracking instead with a four-number scorecard that cannot lie to you.

scenes.narration: Three instruments today. | Scale weight first. | Mirror grade, honest. | Then the tape. | Waist divided by height. | Write all three down. | They will disagree. | They always do. | One of them is the truth. | The other two are weather. | At the end | I tell you | how to grade yourself | like a professional. | Done right, forever.

scenes.label: THE SCORECARD THAT REPLACES THE MIRROR
scenes.narration: Here is the line, and it is a hierarchy. Done right grades body composition with four numbers in a fixed trust order: the waist-to-height ratio first, your current test number second, your step floor and sleep average as the supporting evidence, and the scale and mirror allowed to speak only after the numbers have. The old way inverted the hierarchy daily, letting the moodiest instruments overrule the honest ones, and the predictable result was a man abandoning working systems on the evidence of bathroom lighting. If your three readings from the test disagree today, that disagreement is not a problem to solve. It is the normal state of a recomp in progress, and the scorecard exists precisely to grade it without panic. Keep the three numbers. We are appointing their court.
scenes.sub: tape first, scale last - the hierarchy decides

beats.text: WEIGHT IS JUST THE SHIPPING WEIGHT

scenes.narration: Training your body composition instead of chasing your weight means aiming every habit at the exchange: fat tissue leaving while muscle tissue arrives, ideally at a scale weight that barely moves. The exchange is the product this entire season manufactures. Training signals place the muscle orders, protein delivers, steps and sleep and stress work tilt the fat side of the ledger. Weight, by contrast, is just the shipping weight of the whole operation, rising and falling with water and glycogen that have nothing to do with the cargo. A man who understands the exchange reads a flat month on the scale with a falling ratio as a profitable month, because it was. A man who does not reads it as failure and fires his best employees. The tape audits the exchange monthly because the exchange is monthly, and that single alignment, the right instrument at the right frequency, is the difference between grading and guessing. And one more exchange subtlety for the patient reader of ratios. Early in a recomp, the tape often moves before the mirror because the first fat lost is the deep kind around the waist, the metabolically loud kind, while the surface changes lag behind it. Your best month may photograph like your worst. The scorecard knows. This is why the card reviews the tape first and the photographs quarterly: the order of trust is also the order in which the truth actually arrives.

The scorecard, line by line, so you can build it tonight. Line one: waist-to-height ratio, monthly, the composition verdict. Line two: your rotating test number, push-ups, hang, squat, whichever this month's test was, the signal verdict. Line three: your step floor, the worst day of the week averaged across the month, the background verdict. Line four: your sleep score average, the funding verdict. Four lines, four systems, one page. Review them together on one calm morning a month, because together they diagnose what no single number can: if the ratio stalls, the other three lines point at the failing layer within seconds. Then make at most one adjustment, the one the evidence indicts, and close the book. A scorecard that produces five changes a month is a panic diary with better formatting. One adjustment, monthly, compounded, is how professionals steer anything slow and valuable. A closing word on adjustments, because the review meeting is where scorecards go to die. Change the variable the evidence indicts, change it by the smallest amount that could matter, and give it a full month before judging. Everything else is churn. The men who transform are not the men who found the perfect settings. They are the men who stopped resetting the machine long enough for the settings they had to work.

Photographs get demoted, not fired. Done right keeps one photo set a month, front and side, same light, same distance, same state, then files it away unstudied. Photos are evidence for the quarterly review, where real composition change is actually visible, not a daily verdict to be litigated in the bathroom. Compared quarterly, your photographs will show what the monthly ratios promised, and the two together end the mirror argument permanently: the tape said it first, the photo confirms it later, and the mirror in between is just a place you brush your teeth. This is the emotional dividend of the whole system. You stop asking a moody instrument for permission to continue, and start asking a boring scorecard whether anything needs adjusting. Boring wins. Boring has always won. The mirror was only ever loud, never right on schedule.

lines: is a line on this card.
beats.title: THE WHOLE SYSTEM

beats.text: YOU ARE THE CONTROL ROOM NOW

scenes.narration: Step back and see what the scorecard really is: the entire season on one page. The chest, arm and leg tests became line two. The waist ratio became line one. The step floor and the sleep average became lines three and four, with the stress gap as the card's early-warning light. Twenty-five episodes of tests were never twenty-five separate projects. They were the installation of one control room, instrument by instrument, until the man who once graded himself by a bathroom mirror and a mood now runs his body composition like an engineer: signals in, composition out, reviewed monthly, adjusted singly. That is the real transformation this season sells, and it happens before the visible one. The frame follows the control room. It always has. It just needed someone to build it.
Hang with me one more time. Three rounds, forty-five seconds, thirty seconds of rest. The first test of the next season is already in your hands. Literally. Go.

beats.text: GRADING THE CARD IN A BAD MOOD

scenes.narration: Tonight's assignment is the baseline. One page, four lines, today's honest numbers, dated. Add the photo set under the standard conditions and file it without studying it. Put the monthly review in the calendar as an appointment with the same status as your training anchors. The mistakes to refuse at the door: adding a fifth metric that needs daily attention, which reopens the panic department the card was built to close. Grading the card at midnight in a bad mood, which is the mirror mistake with paperwork. And skipping the baseline because you plan to start properly next month, when next month's entire value is being compared against a baseline written today, by the man you are now, in the body you actually have.

beats.text: WHEN THEY DISAGREE, THE CARD DECIDES

scenes.label: THEN THE FIRST FULL REVIEW
scenes.narration: So, today's disagreement, graded. If the ratio improved while the scale sulked: the exchange is running and you are winning, whatever the mirror said this morning. If the scale dropped and the ratio stalled: tissue you wanted left with the tissue you did not, and protein and signals get the next adjustment. If all three sulked: the card's other lines will name the failing layer at the review, steps, sleep or stress, and one adjustment follows. Put your ratio in the comments, line one of your new scorecard. Just the number. In thirty days the first full review convenes, and for the first time in your life, your body composition will be graded by a court that cannot lie to you.
scenes.sub: exchange running / wrong tissue / layer named - card decides

scenes.narration: Write the baseline tonight, dated, before the day can edit it. Thirty days from now the scorecard holds its first review, and your progress stops being a feeling you argue with and becomes a trend you follow. If this helped, subscribe for the next test.
